words.gloss: sirā (vessel, here blood-carrying vessel; vein, probable); division

hindi: अब इसलिए हम शरीर सम्बन्धी सिराओं यानी वाहिनियों के विभाग की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the bodily division of the sirās (vessels).
notes: sirā = vessel; in this tradition it covers the veins and other blood-carrying vessels (probable); the Sanskrit term is kept. 'śārīra' (bodily) is taken with vibhāga.

words.gloss: ojas (vital essence; doctrinal term, no modern equivalent)

hindi: हृदय से बँधी हुई दस मूलसिराएँ सब अंगों और प्रत्यंगों तक ओज यानी जीवन-सार को ले जाती हैं।
english: Ten root-sirās (mūlasirā), bound to the heart (hṛdaya), carry ojas (vital essence) to all the limbs (aṅga) and sub-limbs (pratyaṅga).

text_flags.why: possible: the long ā between -nyā- and -ojo- looks like a stray vowel; -āni + ojaḥ gives -āny ojo

notes: 'mūlasirā' stands for mūlasirāḥ before h- (āḥ before a voiced sound drops its visarga: regular, no flag). ojas is a doctrinal term (vital essence) with no modern equivalent; it is kept. The two accusatives with nayanti: ojas is what is carried, the limbs and sub-limbs where it is carried to.

hindi: क्योंकि शरीर की चेष्टाएँ उनसे बँधी हैं।
english: For the activities (ceṣṭā) of the body are bound to those.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 2; 'tat' is understood to refer to the ten root-sirās there. 'tatpratibaddhā' for tatpratibaddhāḥ before h-: regular sandhi.

words.gloss: tree; leaf; sevanī (seam, thread; sense uncertain); spreading; like
being dispersed (printed form; possibly vibhajyamānāḥ, being divided)
words.gram: pass. part. vi-√dham, f. nom. pl.

hindi: वे तो दो अङ्गुल, अङ्गुल, आधा अङ्गुल, यव और आधा यव जाकर, वृक्ष के पत्ते की सेवनी जिसका अर्थ अनिश्चित है उसके फैलाव की तरह बिखरती हुई सात सौ हो जाती हैं।
english: But those, having gone two aṅgulas, an aṅgula, half an aṅgula, a yava (barley-grain) and half a yava, being dispersed like the spreading of the sevanī (sense uncertain) of a tree's leaf, become seven hundred.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vidhamyamāna' (being blown apart) is a real word but 'vibhajyamāna' (being divided) fits a count of branches; bha/dha and ja/ma are easily confused in print

notes: 'tāḥ' = the sirās (understood; the branches of the ten root-sirās of unit 2). aṅgula = finger-breadth, yava = barley-grain, both measures; not converted. The sevanī-pratāna simile is not firm: sevanī is 'seam, stitching' elsewhere and the exact picture (leaf veins?) is not stated, so it is kept as printed with the sense marked uncertain. The measures are read as successive stages of the branching; the wording does not say whether length or thickness. Printed 'vidhamyamānāḥ' (dispersed) may be a misreading of vibhajyamānāḥ (divided): bha/dha and ja/ma are close in print; both senses suit 'branching out', so the printed word is kept and flagged as possible. Orthography: -rdd- written -rd- in w.
lines_deva: तास्तु द्व्यंगुलमंगुलमर्द्धंगुलं यवं यवार्द्धं च गत्वा द्रुमपत्रसेवनीप्रतानवद्विधम्यमानाः सप्त शतानि भवंति
lines_iast: tāstu dvyaṃgulamaṃgulamarddhaṃgulaṃ yavaṃ yavārddhaṃ ca gatvā drumapatrasevanīpratānavadvidhamyamānāḥ sapta śatāni bhavaṃti

words.gloss: four; hundred (a set of four hundred)
in the limbs (śākhā, literally branches; the arms and legs, standard)

hindi: उनमें चार सौ शाखाओं यानी हाथ-पैरों में हैं।
english: Of them, four hundred are in the limbs (śākhā).
notes: Copula understood. śākhā = branch; in this body-division the four limbs (arms and legs), standard. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 4 (the seven hundred).

hindi: उनमें सोलह बेधने योग्य नहीं हैं।
english: Among those, sixteen are not to be pierced.
notes: Copula understood. 'tatra' is read as 'among those' (the four hundred of unit 5). vyadh = pierce; in practice venepuncture or bloodletting is meant (probable), but the literal 'pierced' is kept.

hindi: अन्तराधि यानी धड़ में एक सौ छत्तीस।
english: One hundred and thirty-six in the antarādhi (trunk, probable).
notes: 'ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ śatam' is read as a hundred with thirty-six added = 136. antarādhi = the trunk, the part between the limbs and the head: probable. Copula understood. Arithmetic aside: 400 (unit 5) + 136 + 164 (unit 9) = 700 (unit 4). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 5.

hindi: उनमें बाईस।
english: Among those, twenty-two.

text_flags.why: possible, and likely: tatra (as in u6 and u9) gives the number of sirās not to be pierced within the trunk's 136, so 22 does not clash with 136. The trunk lists that name sirās to be guarded add up to 8 (u13) + 2 (u14) + 4 (u16) + 4 (u18) + 14 (u23) = 32, which is dvātriṃśat; dvāviṃśat and dvātriṃśat differ by one letter. Not applied; the printed 22 is translated

notes: Number translated as printed, not corrected. tatra is read as in unit 6 (sixteen not to be pierced) and unit 9 (fifty): 'among those (the 136 of the trunk)', a subset of sirās not to be pierced; this is an inference from the parallel wording, not stated. 22 therefore does not conflict with the 136, but the guarded sirās named in units 13-23 add up to 32 (8 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 14), so the printed dvāviṃśat is probably a misreading of dvātriṃśat; flagged as possible, not applied. Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 7.

hindi: एक सौ चौंसठ ऊपर; उनमें भी पचास।
english: One hundred and sixty-four above; among those also, fifty.
notes: 'catuḥṣaṣṭyadhikaṃ śatam' = a hundred with sixty-four in excess = 164. 'ūrdhvam' = above (the upper part of the body); it is not further defined in the line. What the fifty are is not stated. Copula understood. 400 + 136 + 164 = 700 as in unit 4. Arithmetic check (not stated in the text): the sirās named for guarding in the upper part, units 26-38, give 16 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 7 + 4 + 8 = 50, which suggests the fifty are the ones not to be pierced, as in units 6 and 8; the ear total of 4 in unit 36 is itself an inference.

words.gloss: thigh, leg (sakthi); printed form, locative sg. would be sakthni
jāladharā (name of a vessel, apparently; literally net-bearing; sense uncertain)

hindi: उनमें प्रत्येक सक्थि यानी जाँघ में सौ; उनमें जालधरा को न बेधे।
english: Of them, a hundred in each thigh (sakthi). Among those, one should not pierce the jāladharā,

text_flags.why: possible: the locative singular of sakthi is sakthni (or sakthini); printed 'sakthi' looks like a lost -n-

notes: The printed '|' after śataṃ is a punctuation mark inside the unit; it ends the first clause. 'sakthi' is the thigh or leg; the four limbs would give 4 x 100 = 400 (unit 5), but the line names only sakthi, so 'thigh' is kept as printed and not widened. Printed 'sakthi' is not the usual locative (sakthni): possible slip, flagged. jāladharā: taken as a name of a kind of sirā (apparently, from the context 'not to be pierced'); the literal sense 'net-bearing' is uncertain and nothing is added. GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 11, which supplies further objects of 'na vidhyet'.

hindi: और आड़ी तथा भीतर जाने वाली।
english: and (ones) going across and within.
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete unit 10: 'tiras ca abhyantaragāḥ' are further objects of 'na vidhyet' (not translated as a full sentence here because the verb belongs to unit 10). tiras is taken as an adverb with -gāḥ; 'across' may also mean 'oblique'.

words.gloss: in the śroṇi (hip region, pelvis; standard)
anus (guda; standard); penis (meḍhra; standard); seat, support

hindi: बत्तीस श्रोणि यानी कटि-प्रदेश में, जिनका आश्रय गुद यानी मलद्वार और मेढ्र यानी शिश्न है।
english: Thirty-two in the śroṇi (hip region), having the guda (anus) and meḍhra (penis) as their seat.
notes: Copula understood. Printed meḍhra with an anusvara (meṃḍhra), a variant spelling of meḍhra; normalised in w. 'āśraya' = seat, support; the line does not say more about how they rest.

words.gloss: in the two kaṭīkataruṇas (name of a marma)

hindi: उनमें दो-दो दोनों वंक्षणों यानी जाँघ के मूल में और दोनों कटीकतरुणों में, इस प्रकार आठ; अनुमानित पाठ पर शस्त्र से रक्षा करे।
english: Of them, two each in the two groins (vaṅkṣaṇa) and in the two kaṭīkataruṇas, thus eight; on a conjectural reading, one should guard (them) from the knife (śastra).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śakhato' is not a word; śastrataḥ (from the knife) with rakṣet fits the sense of units 26 and 38; kha/stra confusion

notes: Printed 'śakhato' is not a word. On a conjectural reading it is śastrataḥ (from the knife), as in units 26 and 38 where the same kind of list ends 'śastreṇa na spṛśet' / 'śastreṇa pariharet'; kha for stra is a plausible misreading. The conjecture is hedged in both translations. 'kaṭīkataruṇa' is a marma name in this tradition (probable); marma = vital spot (doctrinal term). 'aṣṭau' = 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 over the groins and the kaṭīkataruṇas.
lines_deva: तासां द्वे द्वे वंक्षणयोः कटीकतरुणयोश्चेत्यष्टौशखतो रक्षेत्
lines_iast: tāsāṃ dve dve vaṃkṣaṇayoḥ kaṭīkataruṇayoścetyaṣṭauśakhato rakṣet

words.gloss: pārśvasandhi (name of a marma); name, called

hindi: सोलह दोनों पार्श्वों यानी बगलों में; उन दोनों में एक-एक ऊपर जाने वाली, पार्श्वसन्धि नाम वाली।
english: Sixteen in the two sides (pārśva); of those two, one each going upward, named pārśvasandhi.
notes: Elliptical: the accusatives suggest that a verb such as rakṣet (unit 13) is understood; none is supplied. 'tayoḥ' = of the two sides. pārśvasandhi is a marma name in this tradition (probable). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 13.

hindi: पीठ में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the back (pṛṣṭha).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें पृष्ठवंश यानी रीढ़ के दोनों ओर दो-दो ऊपर जाने वाली; वे चार हैं।
english: Of them, on both sides of the pṛṣṭhavaṃśa (spine), two and two going upward; those are four.
notes: Copula understood in the last clause. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 15.
lines_deva: तासां पृष्ठवंशमुभयतो द्वे द्वे ऊर्ध्वगामिन्यौ ताश्चतस्रः
lines_iast: tāsāṃ pṛṣṭhavaṃśamubhayato dve dve ūrdhvagāminyau tāścatasraḥ

hindi: पेट में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the belly (udara).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें मेढ्र यानी शिश्न के ऊपर, रोमराजी यानी रोमों की रेखा के दोनों ओर, दो-दो; वे भी चार हैं।
english: Of them, above the meḍhra (penis), on both sides of the romarājī (line of body hair), two and two; those also are four.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'omarājī' is not a word; the ra of romarājī (line of body hair) has dropped out in print

notes: Printed 'upariomarājīm': the ra of romarājī is lost (the Devanagari shows a bare vowel sign); romarājī, the line of body hair, is a known word; near certain. 'tā api' for tāḥ api: regular sandhi. Printed meṃḍhra = meḍhra. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 17.
lines_deva: तासां मेंढ्रस्योपरिोमराजीमुभयतो द्वे द्वे ताअपि चतस्रः
lines_iast: tāsāṃ meṃḍhrasyopariomarājīmubhayato dve dve tāapi catasraḥ

hindi: वक्ष यानी छाती में चालीस।
english: Forty in the chest (vakṣas).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें दो हृदय में।
english: Of them, two in the heart (hṛdaya).
notes: Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 19 (the chest).

words.gloss: stanamūla (breast-root, a named place); stanarohita (a named place; sense of rohita uncertain)

hindi: और दो-दो स्तनमूलों और स्तनरोहितों में।
english: And two and two in the stanamūlas and the stanarohitas.
notes: Copula understood. stanamūla and stanarohita are names of marmas in this tradition (probable); the line does not say so, so they are kept as names. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 20. Arithmetic check (not stated): the chest sirās to be guarded come to 14 (unit 23) only if 'dve dve' means two on each side in each of the stanamūla and stanarohita: 2 (heart) + 4 + 4 + 4 (apastambha, apalāpa) = 14. The translation keeps the plural place names and does not decide this.

words.gloss: apastambha (a named place; name of a marma in this tradition, probable)
apalāpa (a named place; on a conjectural reading)

hindi: एक-एक अपस्तम्भों और अपलापों में, अनुमानित पाठ पर; इस प्रकार।
english: One each in the apastambhas and the apalāpas (on a conjectural reading), thus.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ālāpa' (talk) is not a body place; apalāpa (a known name beside apastambha) fits with the p lost

notes: Printed 'ālāpa' (talk) does not suit a list of body places; apalāpa, a name in the same series (probable), with the p lost, fits. The conjecture is hedged in both translations. The avagraha after -ā (ekaikā'pastaṃbhā-) is a print habit (ā + a). Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 21.

hindi: वे चौदह हैं।
english: Those are fourteen.
notes: Copula understood. 'tāḥ' = those counted in units 20-22 (appears). GROUPING: appears to complete units 19-22 (the chest total of forty is given in unit 19; fourteen is a part). Arithmetic: 14 = 2 (heart) + 4 (stanamūlas) + 4 (stanarohitas) + 4 (apastambhas and apalāpas) if 'dve dve' in unit 21 gives two on each side; this is an inference, the print gives only the total.

hindi: ग्रीवा यानी गर्दन में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the neck (grīvā).
notes: Copula understood.

words.gloss: marma (vital spot; doctrinal term); name, called

hindi: उनमें चार और आठ मर्म यानी जीवन-स्थल नाम वाली हैं।
english: Of them, four and eight are named marma (vital spot).
notes: Copula understood. marma is a doctrinal term (vital spot) and is kept. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 24.

words.gloss: in the two kṛkāṭikās (name of a marma, at the junction of head and neck behind; probable)
in the two vidhuras (name of a marma, behind the ear; probable)

hindi: दो दोनों कृकाटिकाओं में और दो दोनों विधुरों में, इस प्रकार सोलह; शस्त्र से न छुए।
english: Two in the two kṛkāṭikās and two in the two vidhuras, thus sixteen; one should not touch (them) with the knife (śastra).
notes: Both names are marma names in this tradition (probable). 'sixteen' = 4 + 8 of unit 25 plus these 2 + 2. Printed 'dvevidhurayoriti' = dve vidhurayoḥ iti. GROUPING: appears to complete unit 25.
lines_deva: द्वे कृकाटिकयोर्द्वेविधुरयोरिति षोडश शस्त्रेण न स्पृशेत्
lines_iast: dve kṛkāṭikayordvevidhurayoriti ṣoḍaśa śastreṇa na spṛśet

hindi: दोनों हनु यानी जबड़ों में सोलह; उनमें दो सन्धि से सम्बद्ध।
english: In the two jaws (hanu), sixteen; of them, two connected with the joint (sandhi).
notes: Copula understood. Which joint is not stated (the jaw joint is the natural but unstated reading).

hindi: जिह्वा यानी जीभ में सोलह।
english: Sixteen in the tongue (jihvā).
notes: Printed 'jivhā' is a letter reversal of jihvā (recorded once; normalised in w). Copula understood.

words.gloss: speech; setting in motion, bringing about

hindi: उनके नीचे दो रस यानी स्वाद का बोध करने वाली और दो वाणी को प्रवृत्त करने वाली; वे चार हैं।
english: Below them, two perceiving taste (rasa) and two setting speech in motion; those are four.
notes: 'tāsām adhaḥ' is read as 'below them'; 'of them, underneath' is the alternative. Copula understood in the last clause. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 28 (the tongue).

hindi: नासा यानी नाक में चौबीस।
english: Twenty-four in the nose (nāsā).
notes: Copula understood.

hindi: उनमें दो गन्ध का बोध करने वाली, और उन्हीं में से एक तालु में; इस प्रकार तीन।
english: Of them, two perceiving smell (gandha); and of those very ones, one in the palate (tālu); thus three.
notes: Elliptical: 'ekām' is accusative with no verb; none is supplied. 'tāsām eva' = of those very ones (the 24 of the nose, appears). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 30.
lines_deva: तासां द्वे गंधवेदिन्यौ तासामेव च तालुन्येकामिति तिस्रः
lines_iast: tāsāṃ dve gaṃdhavedinyau tāsāmeva ca tālunyekāmiti tisraḥ

hindi: दोनों नेत्रों में छप्पन।
english: Fifty-six in the two eyes (netra).
notes: Copula understood. Printed 'ṣaṭpaṃcāśannetrayoḥ' = ṣaṭpañcāśat netrayoḥ (t before n becomes n: regular).

words.gloss: in the two apāṅgas (outer corners of the eye; standard)

hindi: उन दोनों में उन्मेष और निमेष की क्रियाएँ: दो, दो; और दो दोनों अपाङ्गों में; इस प्रकार छह।
english: Of those two, the two actions of opening (unmeṣa) and closing (nimeṣa): two, two; and two in the two apāṅgas (outer corners of the eye); thus six.
notes: Elliptical, and the distribution is not firm: 'unmeṣanimeṣakriye dve dve' is read as two for the action of opening and two for the action of closing (2 + 2), with 2 more in the apāṅgas, thus six; the dual 'kriye' could also qualify the first 'dve'. apāṅga is also a marma name in this tradition (probable). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 32.
lines_deva: तयोरुन्मेषनिमेषक्रिये द्वे द्वे द्वे चापांगयोरिति षट्
lines_iast: tayorunmeṣanimeṣakriye dve dve dve cāpāṃgayoriti ṣaṭ

hindi: नासा और नेत्रों तक गई हुई वे तो ललाट में साठ हैं।
english: Those that go to the nose and eyes, however, are sixty in the forehead (lalāṭa).
notes: Copula understood. The line does not say whether the sixty are additional to the 24 of the nose and 56 of the eyes; no relation is stated or assumed. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 33. Arithmetic check: neck 24 + jaws 16 + tongue 16 + nose 24 + eyes 56 + ears 16 + head 12 = 164 (unit 9), so the sixty in the forehead are not additional to the 24 of the nose and 56 of the eyes; they appear to be sirās going to the nose and eyes that lie in the forehead.

words.gloss: hair; end; gone along to (keśānta: end of the hair, probably the hair-line)
in the two āvartas (whorl; a named place, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)
in the sthapanī (a named place, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)

hindi: उनमें चार केशान्त यानी सम्भवतः केशों के अन्त तक जाने वाली, दो दोनों आवर्तों में और एक स्थपनी में; इस प्रकार सात।
english: Of them, four going along to the keśānta (end of the hair, probably the hair-line); two in the two āvartas; and one in the sthapanī; thus seven.

text_flags.why: possible: keśānta + anugatāḥ joins as keśāntānugatāḥ (long ā); the printed short -a- may be a lost length mark or a lost anusvara (keśāntam anugatāḥ)

notes: Printed 'keśāṃtanugatāḥ': a + a should join as ā (keśāntānugatāḥ), or keśāntam anugatāḥ with m lost; the sense is the same; flagged as possible. keśānta = hair-line is probable, not stated. Copula understood. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 34.
lines_deva: तासां केशांतनुगताश्चतस्रो द्वे आवर्तयोरेका च स्थपन्यामिति सप्त
lines_iast: tāsāṃ keśāṃtanugatāścatasro dve āvartayorekā ca sthapanyāmiti sapta

hindi: दोनों कर्णों में सोलह; उनमें दो शब्द को वहन करने वाली; वही दोनों शंखों यानी कनपटियों में भी; उनमें दो शंख की सन्धि तक गई हुई।
english: In the two ears (karṇa), sixteen; of them, two carrying sound (śabda); those very two also in the two śaṅkhas (temples); of them, two gone to the joint (sandhi) of the temple.
notes: Printed 'evaca' joins eva and ca (spacing slip, no flag). The second and third clauses are elliptical; copula understood. The relation of 'those very two' to the two in the temples is as the Sanskrit states it and is not explained further. śaṅkha = temple of the head (the same word means conch); standard here. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 35. 'te eva' = those very two (the sound-carriers), not two additional ones: this agrees with the arithmetic of unit 9 (fifty guarded in the upper part needs 4 for the ears: 2 sound-carriers + 2 at the temple joint). Inference, not stated.
lines_deva: कर्णयोः षोडश तासां शब्दवाहिन्यौ द्वे ते एवच शंखयोः तासां शंखसंधिगते द्वे
lines_iast: karṇayoḥ ṣoḍaśa tāsāṃ śabdavāhinyau dve te evaca śaṃkhayoḥ tāsāṃ śaṃkhasaṃdhigate dve

hindi: सिर में बारह।
english: Twelve in the head (mūrdhan).
notes: Printed 'mūrddhani' (-rdd-) normalised to mūrdhani in w. Copula understood.

words.gloss: in the two utkṣepas (a named place on the head, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)
in the sīmantas (a named place; literally parting; name of marmas in this tradition, probable)
in the adhipati (a named place, name of a marma in this tradition, probable)

hindi: उनमें दो दोनों उत्क्षेपों में, एक-एक सीमन्तों में, एक अधिपति में; इस प्रकार आठ; शस्त्र से परिहार करे।
english: Of them, two in the two utkṣepas; one each in the sīmantas; one in the adhipati; thus eight: one should avoid (them) with the knife (śastra).
notes: The accusatives ekaikām and ekām have no governing verb in the clause; none is supplied. The numbers fit 2 + 5 + 1 = 8 only if there are five sīmantas, which the line does not state. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 37 (the head).

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, इसी प्रकार छोटी, टेढ़ी, मिली हुई, गुँथी हुई और जोड़ों में, शस्त्र-कर्म के योग्य नहीं हैं।
english: Likewise (on a conjectural reading of the first word), the small, crooked, intermingled and knotted ones, and those in the joints, are not to be dealt with by the knife (śastra).

text_flags.why: possible: 'na tathā' would clash with the following negative aśastrakṛtyāḥ (double negative); 'tathā' (likewise) opens a further class naturally; the na may be a stray stroke

notes: Printed 'natathā': read na + tathā it would give a double negative with aśastrakṛtyāḥ; the stray na may be an extra stroke before tathā (likewise), the natural opener of a further class. Conjectural, flagged as possible and hedged in both translations. 'saṃkīrṇā' for saṃkīrṇāḥ before g-: regular sandhi. 'grathita' is a recognised variant of granthita; no flag. 'kṛtya' = to be done; aśastrakṛtya = not to be done with the knife. Copula understood. The nouns are not stated (sirās understood). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 38.
lines_deva: नतथा क्षुद्रिकाः कुटिलाः संकीर्णा ग्रथिताः संधिषु चाशस्त्रकृत्याः
lines_iast: natathā kṣudrikāḥ kuṭilāḥ saṃkīrṇā grathitāḥ saṃdhiṣu cāśastrakṛtyāḥ

hindi: उनमें अपने-अपने अनुसार, चौथे अंश के विभाग से, पचहत्तर अधिक सौ का समूह वात और रक्त का वहन करता है।
english: Of them, each according to its own, by a division into fourth parts, a set of a hundred with seventy-five in addition carries Vāta and blood (anila-rakta).
notes: 175 is a quarter of the 700 of unit 4. 'anilaraktam' is read as a dvandva, Vāta and blood; a reading as one compound (blood with Vāta) is possible and is not decided. anila = wind, here Vāta. The sentence is not extended beyond what is printed.
lines_deva: तासां यथास्वं तुर्यांशविभागेन पंचसप्तत्यधिकं शतकमनिलरक्तं वहति
lines_iast: tāsāṃ yathāsvaṃ turyāṃśavibhāgena paṃcasaptatyadhikaṃ śatakamanilaraktaṃ vahati

hindi: यह विभाग पित्त, श्लेष्मा यानी कफ और शुद्ध रक्त में भी है।
english: This division is also in Pitta, śleṣman (Kapha) and pure blood.
notes: Copula understood. 'eṣa' for eṣaḥ before v-: regular. śleṣman = Kapha (standard). What exactly the division of 175 is here (one quarter each for Vāta with blood, Pitta, śleṣman and pure blood) is suggested by the arithmetic with unit 40 but is not stated, so nothing is added. GROUPING: appears to complete unit 40.
